biological.citation: TMEM63 proteins function as monomeric high-threshold mechanosensitive ion channels (PMID: 37543036)
biological.summary: Cryo-EM structures of TMEM63B revealed a monomeric configuration with a single highly restricted pore, distinct from the homodimeric architecture of plant OSCA channels. Functional analyses confirmed TMEM63B is a bona fide mechanosensitive ion channel with small conductance and high activation thresholds. The intracellular linker IL2 mediates dimerization in OSCAs but drives monomeric assembly in TMEM63B, affecting mechanosensitivity.

biological.citation: Stretch-activated ion channel TMEM63B associates with developmental and epileptic encephalopathies and progressive neurodegeneration (PMID: 37421948)
biological.summary: Six disease-associated TMEM63B variants (including recurrent p.Val44Met) were modeled in transfected Neuro2a cells, demonstrating inward leak cation currents under isotonic conditions and impaired responses to hypo-osmotic challenge, as well as disrupted Ca2+ transients. Ectopic expression of p.Val44Met and p.Gly580Cys variants in Drosophila caused early death. The study established TMEM63B-associated DEE as a clinicopathological entity with progressive neurodegeneration, early-onset epilepsy, and hematological abnormalities in 17 unrelated individuals.

biological.citation: Mechanosensitive channels TMEM63A and TMEM63B mediate lung inflation-induced surfactant secretion (PMID: 38127458)
biological.summary: Loss of TMEM63A/B in mice resulted in atelectasis and respiratory failure due to deficient pulmonary surfactant secretion. TMEM63A/B were predominantly localized at the limiting membrane of lamellar bodies in alveolar type 2 epithelial cells, and their activation during cell stretch facilitated surfactant and ATP release. Released ATP evoked Ca2+ signaling that potentiated further exocytic fusion of lamellar bodies.

biological.citation: Phospholipid scrambling induced by an ion channel/metabolite transporter complex (PMID: 39217145)
biological.summary: CRISPR sgRNA library screening identified TMEM63B as a phospholipid scrambling (PLS)-inducing factor upon Ca2+ stimulation. Biochemical screening revealed that TMEM63B forms a heterodimer with the thiamine transporter SLC19A2, and deletion of either gene decreased PLS activity. Human disease-related TMEM63B mutants induced constitutive PLS, and the Ca2+-activated K+ channel KCNN4 was identified as an additional PLS-regulating factor in this complex.

biological.citation: Membrane structure-responsive lipid scrambling by TMEM63B to control plasma membrane lipid distribution (PMID: 39424995)
biological.summary: TMEM63B functions as a membrane structure-responsive lipid scramblase localized at the plasma membrane and lysosomes, activating bidirectional lipid translocation in response to changes in membrane curvature and thickness. TMEM63B deficiency alters phosphatidylcholine and sphingomyelin distributions in the plasma membrane. The disease-associated V44M substitution confers constitutive scramblase activity, disrupting plasma membrane phospholipid asymmetry; cryo-EM structures revealed open and closed conformations with a lipid translocation pathway.

biological.citation: Expression and localization of the mechanosensitive/osmosensitive ion channel TMEM63B in the mouse urinary tract (PMID: 38724885)
biological.summary: Using HA-tagged Tmem63b reporter mice and immunofluorescence confocal microscopy, TMEM63B protein was detected in proximal tubule epithelial cells, intercalated cells of the collecting duct, and thick ascending limb epithelial cells of the kidney. In the lower urinary tract, TMEM63B was expressed in urothelium lining the renal pelvis, ureters, bladder, and urethra, as well as in seminal vesicles, vas deferens, lateral prostate, and vaginal epithelium.

biological.citation: A splicing-dependent ER retention signal regulates surface expression of the mechanosensitive TMEM63B cation channel (PMID: 36496074)
biological.summary: Brain-specific alternative splicing of exon 4 in TMEM63B produces a short isoform (lacking exon 4) that is the major brain isoform and shows enhanced surface expression and stronger responses to hypoosmotic stimulation compared to the long isoform. Mutagenesis identified an RXR-type ER retention signal within exon 4 that mediates COPI retrieval, retaining the long isoform in the ER. Long and short TMEM63B isoforms can form heterodimers, with the long isoform reducing surface expression of the short isoform.

biological.citation: Mechanical signaling through membrane tension induces somal translocation during neuronal migration (PMID: 39707024)
biological.summary: Using the membrane tension sensor Flipper-TR and scanning ion conductance microscopy, leading process extension during neuronal migration was shown to increase plasma membrane tension, which activated Tmem63b and triggered Ca2+ influx. This Ca2+ influx led to actomyosin activation at the rear of the cell, driving somal translocation. Blockade of this Tmem63b-mediated signaling pathway inhibited neuronal migration in three-dimensional environments.

biological.citation: The TMEM63B Channel Facilitates Intestinal Motility and Enhances Proliferation of Intestinal Stem Cells (PMID: 39513891)
biological.summary: TMEM63B is expressed in intestinal stem cells and its deletion in these cells decelerated intestinal motility, impaired digestion, attenuated intestinal stem cell proliferation, and exacerbated DSS-induced colitis in mice. These findings identify TMEM63B as a mechanosensitive channel regulating gastrointestinal motility and intestinal stem cell homeostasis. The channel likely responds to osmotic pressure changes within the intestinal lumen.

biological.citation: ASHG 2019 - Human and mouse essentiality screens as a resource for disease gene discovery (P. Cacheiro et al.)
biological.summary: Integrating IMPC knockout mouse viability data with human intolerance-to-variation scores, TMEM63B was identified as a developmental lethal gene highly intolerant to variation. Screening of unsolved developmental disorder cases identified potentially pathogenic de novo variants in TMEM63B in multiple patients exhibiting intellectual disability and neurological/movement phenotypes partially modeled by the IMPC mouse knockout. This highlighted TMEM63B as a novel candidate gene for intellectual disability.
biological.sample_size: 163 developmental lethal genes screened; multiple independent disease sequencing consortia
